_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on the Elasticsearch egg in pterodactyl/application-eggs (MIT).
name: Elasticsearch
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Elasticsearch is a search and analytics engine, run here as a single node with security on. Its REST API is on the server's port over HTTPS; the elastic user's password is the one you set, or one made and printed when it first starts.
startup: if ! ./bin/elasticsearch-keystore list 2>/dev/null | grep -qx bootstrap.password; then p="$ELASTIC_PASSWORD"; if [ -z "$p" ]; then p=$(head -c 18 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d "/+="); echo "$p" > elastic-password.txt; echo "The elastic user's password is $p (saved in elastic-password.txt)."; fi; [ -f config/elasticsearch.keystore ] || ./bin/elasticsearch-keystore create >/dev/null; printf "%s" "$p" | ./bin/elasticsearch-keystore add -x bootstrap.password; fi; h=$(( {{SERVER_MEMORY}} / 5 + {{SERVER_MEMORY}} / 5 )); export ES_JAVA_OPTS="-Xms${h}m -Xmx${h}m"; exec ./bin/elasticsearch -E http.port={{SERVER_PORT}} -E network.host=0.0.0.0 -E discovery.type=single-node

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Elasticsearch: downloads the release for the chosen version from Elastic
# and checks its checksum. Your settings (config), indices (data), logs and
# plugins are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
# Downloads unpack in a folder in the server's (the install's /tmp is
# small), removed when the script ends.
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
rm -rf .raptor-new
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "This server's CPU ($(uname -m)) isn't supported." ;;
esac
put_release() {
    local new=$1 e; shift
    local keep=" $* "
    if [ -f .raptor-files ]; then
        while IFS= read -r e; do
            if [ -n "$e" ] && [ ! -e "$new/$e" ] && [ "${keep#* "$e" }" = "$keep" ]; then rm -rf -- "./$e"; fi
        done < .raptor-files
    fi
    : > .raptor-files.new
    while IFS= read -r e; do
        if [ "${keep#* "$e" }" != "$keep" ] && [ -e "./$e" ]; then
            if [ -d "$new/$e" ]; then cp -rn "$new/$e/." "./$e/" || true; fi
        else
            rm -rf -- "./$e"
            mv "$new/$e" "./$e"
        fi
        echo "$e" >> .raptor-files.new
    done < <(find "$new" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -printf '%f\n')
    mv -f .raptor-files.new .raptor-files
    rm -rf "$new"
}

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
if [ "$want" = latest ]; then
    tag=$(gh-release tag elastic/elasticsearch latest) || fail "GitHub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
    version="${tag#v}"
else
    version="${want#v}"
fi
case "$arch" in amd64) es_arch=x86_64 ;; arm64) es_arch=aarch64 ;; esac
name="elasticsearch-$version-linux-$es_arch.tar.gz"
base="https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/elasticsearch/$name"
code=$(curl -sSL -o $work/es.sha512 -w '%{http_code}' "$base.sha512") || fail "Elastic can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
[ "$code" = 404 ] && fail "Elasticsearch has no version $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 8.19.0."
[ "$code" = 200 ] || fail "Elastic can't be reached right now (HTTP $code). Reinstall to try again."
sum=$(cut -d' ' -f1 $work/es.sha512)

if [ -f "lib/elasticsearch-$version.jar" ]; then
    echo "Elasticsearch $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Elasticsearch $version"
    curl -fsSL -o $work/es.tar.gz "$base" || fail "The download failed ($base). Reinstall to try again."
    [ "$(sha512sum $work/es.tar.gz | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ] || { rm -f $work/es.tar.gz; fail "The download didn't match its checksum. Reinstall to try again."; }
    mkdir .raptor-new
    tar -xzf $work/es.tar.gz -C .raptor-new --strip-components=1
    rm -f $work/es.tar.gz
    put_release .raptor-new config data logs plugins
fi
mkdir -p data logs plugins
echo "Installed Elasticsearch $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Elasticsearch version to install, such as 8.19.0, or latest. Indices can't be moved back to an older version.

variables.name: Elastic password
variables.description: The password for the elastic user, used when it first starts. Leave it empty to have one made, printed in the console and saved in elastic-password.txt.
